K'gari是由漫长地质历史中的风力和海洋沉积形成的世界最大沙岛，拥有建立在沙地: K'gari, the world's largest sand island formed by wind and marine sedimentation over a long geological history, is home to tall rainforests growing on sand, white silica-sand freshwater lakes, and long beaches facing the Pacific Ocean. Further south, Mulgumpin (Moreton Island) is known for its shipwreck reef cluster, bay sunsets, and managed wild dolphin encounters. There is no regular direct ferry to either island; this file is a user-designated two-island feature, and actual travel requires segmented transfers via the Queensland mainland.

US-395沿内华达山脉东侧雨影区纵向延伸，干燥荒漠与海拔四千米级雪峰之间形成剧: US-395 runs north–south along the rain shadow on the eastern side of the Sierra Nevada, creating a dramatic landscape contrast between dry desert and snow peaks rising to around four thousand metres. The tufa towers of Mono Lake rise like an alien castle from alkaline waters, the volcanic remains at Mammoth Lakes preserve geometric basalt columns, high mountain lakes in autumn are ringed by golden aspens, and at the southern end the natural stone arches of the Alabama Hills frame Mount Whitney. This entry organises the designated scenic highway into a continuous self-drive corridor of several hundred kilometres, rather than a single city. Most breathtaking of all is the giant balancing rock, the "Hanging Stone", weighing some six hundred tonnes and poised at the edge of a sheer valley mouth; every July the subalpine meadows bloom with orange-red globeflowers and violets, and in September the larches dye Artist's Lake golden, forming a magnificent, ever-changing mountain visual corridor.

Unlike the Antarctic mainland, which can only be reached by an expensive ship voyage, the Falklands have weekly flights direct from Santiago / Punta Arenas in Chile, then bright-red FIGAS inter-island aircraft hop between the grass airstrips of the outer islands: watch two thousand king penguins strolling a Caribbean-like white-sand beach at Volunteer Point, photograph king, gentoo, Magellanic and rockhopper penguins in a single frame on Saunders Island, see penguins wandering through silvery-white iris meadows in midsummer on Carcass Island, and come face to face with tens of thousands of black-browed albatrosses circling the cliffs on West Point Island. The best season is from late October to March; in the deep winter of May to August many outer-island lodges close and the South Atlantic brings frequent violent winds and cold rain.

Between about ten thousand and five thousand years ago, when the Sahara was still a "Green Sahara" of rivers, lakes and open woodland, ancient people carved and painted more than 15,000 rock images of giraffes, hippos, herded cattle and mysterious round-headed figures among a maze of hundreds of wind-eroded sandstone pillars; today, below the plateau lie the blood-deep crimson sand waves of Tadrart Rouge, black mushroom rock towers rising from the ground, natural giant-stone triumphal arches, and the prehistoric "Weeping Cow" engraving that Sahara photographers dream of most.

在埃塞俄比亚高地云雾深处，藏着非洲中世纪建筑史上最不可思议的双重奇迹：十二世纪扎: Deep in the clouds of the Ethiopian highlands lies the most incredible double miracle in medieval African architecture: in the 12th century, the Zagwe dynasty at Lalibela carved eleven underground temples top-down out of an entire mountain range of reddish-brown volcanic tuff, crowned by the cross-shaped Church of Saint George, unmatched in the world; west across the Amhara highlands lie 17th-century imperial Gondar's stone castle complex and churches with angel-painted wooden ceilings, finally converging on Lake Tana's papyrus wetlands and the thundering Tis Issat Falls of the Blue Nile.
在威德尔海西侧海冰终年厚重盘踞的雪丘岛南岸固定冰上，栖息着地球上最靠北、也是南极: On the fast ice off the southern shore of Snow Hill Island, where heavy sea ice lingers year-round on the western Weddell Sea, lives the northernmost large emperor penguin breeding colony (about 4,000 pairs) and the only one accessible in the Antarctic Peninsula region. Because sea ice blocks all regular vessels, only in early summer from late October to early December do a few professional icebreaking expedition ships with twin helicopters (such as PC5/PC6-class expedition vessels) push through the ice to offshore of Snow Hill Island, then fly explorers by helicopter to a safe landing zone a few kilometres from the colony, from where they trek through snow to approach the fluffy grey-and-white emperor chicks and their tall, elegant parents. The island's north cape also preserves the wooden hut (HSM 38) where Swedish explorer Nordenskjöld overwintered for two years in 1902. In Deep Winter (May–September) the sea is fully ice-locked with day-and-night blizzards, and there is absolutely no commercial expedition activity.

More than forty sharp-angled pyramids crowd among rolling dunes, with almost no tour-group noise to be heard, as wind-blown sand grains sweep across 3,000-year-old relief chapels and broken desert columns; extending southwest and northwest to the sacred mountain of Jebel Barkal, the ancient city of Naga and the Nile's Sixth Cataract, they sketch the portrait of Africa's most underestimated lost empire.

The entire island of São Tomé was shaped by violent submarine basaltic volcanic eruptions, among which Pico Cão Grande—a 300-meter-plus volcanic phonolite needle soaring abruptly from the southern tropical palm rainforest—resembles an alien stone tower piercing the clouds; the northern coast is encircled by the Blue Lagoon's baobabs, the wave-churning basalt 'Hell's Mouth', colonial-era cocoa plantations, and the equatorial reef rocks at the foot of Rolas Island.

In the 16th century, monks used local materials to stack glacial giant granite boulders weighing up to ten tons, building a Kremlin fortress over ten meters high and a freshwater canal network connecting the entire island; the outer periphery of the island even conceals prehistoric stone labyrinth circles, while every year between July and August, schools of wild beluga whales reliably swim to the shallow waters of Cape Beluzhy for calving, presenting an isolated island miracle where the sacred and the wild intertwine.

Autumn green light curtains reflect in deep blue waters, while frigid winters create a massive color contrast of a green firmament and silver snowfields over the frozen Great Slave Lake. Before the autumn harvest in September, golden ridges climb from the valley floor to wooden hillside houses, with morning mist moving slowly along the mountain waist. Traversing south across red scoria hills leads to Kerið Crater and extraordinarily vivid glacial blue waterfalls.

Frigiliana is located about 150–160 road kilometers from Ronda; this file treats it as an independent cross-regional extension stop rather than an intra-city attraction in Ronda, according to the designated list.
